note.note:
History:
• 34-year-old female (Sarah Smith, DOB reported as 20-Apr-1980; clinician repeated 1983 – conflict noted)  
• Chief complaint: Acute onset shortness of breath while seated watching TV, began ≈1 hour prior to call.  
• First episode; no prior similar events.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Dry cough started yesterday, no sputum.  
  – Palpitations (“my heart, it’s really going”).  
  – Chest soreness on deep inspiration; no constant chest pain.  
• No limb swelling, hemoptysis, fever, or recent viral illness reported.  
• Context/Risk factors: 4 weeks post-cesarean section; currently caring for newborn.  
• No current medications except intermittent codeine for postoperative pain (none taken for ≈1 week).

Past Medical History:
• Recent cesarean section (4 weeks ago).  
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medication: Codeine – dose/route/frequency not documented; last use ≈1 week ago.  
• Allergy: Ibuprofen – reaction undocumented.  
• Family history: Mother with history of leg clots (patient volunteered).  
• No other medications, hospitalizations, or conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-visit—limited)  
• Patient alert, speaking in full sentences.  
• Radial pulse count: 30 beats during timed interval; physician interpreted as “slightly fast.” (Exact rate not documented.)  
• No report of chest wall swelling, leg pain/swelling, or throat swelling.  
• No other vitals or physical findings provided.

Impression:
Postpartum dyspnea with mild tachycardia – possible pulmonary embolism.

Management Plan:
• Advised immediate hospital evaluation for suspected clot (pulmonary embolism) given recent C-section and acute dyspnea.  
• Discussed options: ambulance vs. self-transport; patient opted to self-present to hospital promptly, bringing supplies for baby.  
• Instructed to withhold codeine until evaluated.  
• Provided education on clot risk and potential hospital treatments (e.g., anticoagulation).  
• No prescriptions issued during call.

Patient Summary:
Ms. Smith, 4 weeks post-cesarean, developed sudden dyspnea and palpitations without significant chest pain. Given postpartum status and acute presentation, clinician suspects pulmonary embolism and directed her to attend hospital immediately for definitive assessment and management.

Key Takeaways:
• Go to the nearest hospital as soon as possible today.  
• Do not take further codeine or other pain medication before evaluation.  
• Bring necessary items for the baby and inform staff about recent C-section.

Next Steps:
• ED/acute care assessment: vitals, ECG, D-dimer, chest imaging/CT-PA, coagulation profile.  
• Initiate anticoagulation if PE confirmed.  
• Arrange postpartum follow-up with obstetrics and primary care after hospital discharge.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: complete vital signs, detailed reaction to ibuprofen, full medication reconciliation, obstetric/postpartum details, smoking status, social history.  
• Internal conflicts: DOB stated as 20-Apr-1980 by patient; clinician repeated 1983 (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: clear audio, minimal background noise; adequate for clinical documentation.
